$comment: This repository's own profile, so the toolkit is held to its own gate while being developed.
Tracked, unlike the others: it names only a public repo and public commands, and it doubles as
the one worked example in the repository, and the only profile here that actually runs.
Matched on '/dotagents' rather than 'bwkw/dotagents' so it follows the repository into forks and
clones -- it matches both URL forms (https://host/owner/dotagents.git and host:owner/dotagents).
Pinning one owner meant every fork resolved no profile and the gate passed in silence, which is
the failure this profile exists to prevent, on the repository that ships the gate.
The cost is accepted deliberately: an unrelated repository whose name merely starts with
'dotagents' also matches, and its checks then fail loudly because these commands are not there.
Loudly wrong beats silently open -- the ordering the whole gate is built on.

The `paths` on twelve of these are chosen so that NO plausible change set empties the gate. `skills-lint` and `da-review-all-canvas-contract` deliberately have none: they read skills/ and docs, so a documentation-only change still runs something. That is not politeness -- when every gating check declines, the gate BLOCKS with kind not_checked, so a profile that can be emptied is a profile that halts on its most common change.

spec_system.$comment: docs/plans/ is NOT this: that holds the 🧱 landing plans, which scripts/loop.sh discovers by their 'What gates it' header. The implementation plan is what writing-plans produces, and loop.sh:plan_files() looks for it here.

checks.cmd: for f in scripts/*.sh hooks/*.sh; do bash -n "$f" || exit 1; done

checks.when: docs/loops.md's halt-reason table and the strings loop.sh actually writes must stay the same set. The suite is in check.sh; the gate has to run it too, or a divergence lands whenever nobody types check.sh.
always -- the gate is the one component that must fail closed, so its tests gate every turn

checks.cmd: perl -ne 'close ARGV if eof; next if /^\s*#/; exit 1 if /\$[A-Za-z_]\w*[^\x00-\x7F]/' scripts/*.sh hooks/*.sh
checks.when: bash 3.2 under a UTF-8 locale absorbs a full-width character following an unbraced $var into the variable name, so the lookup is unbound and the run dies. macOS ships 3.2, so this passed on Linux and locally under the C locale and failed only on the macOS CI runner. Brace it as ${var}. No leading `!` unlike no-bash4: grep signals 'found' with exit 0, perl here signals it with exit 1, and negating turned a clean tree red.
macOS ships bash 3.2; these pass on Linux and fail there

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");for(const f of fs.readdirSync("templates"))if(f.endsWith(".json"))JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("templates/"+f,"utf8"));for(const f of fs.readdirSync("profiles"))if(f.endsWith(".json"))JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("profiles/"+f,"utf8"))'

checks.when: Claude Code does not read AGENTS.md, so if the symlink becomes a regular file the always-loaded layer silently drifts

checks.cmd: ! git ls-files -s scripts/*.sh hooks/*.sh | awk '$1!="100755"{print;f=1} END{exit !f}'
checks.when: every suite invokes through `bash <file>`, so a lost +x bit passes all of them and breaks `scripts/gate.sh arm`
always -- the driver decides unattended whether work may reach a PR, so the checks that stop it are not optional
da-review-all must keep producing its one-page overview in whichever container the host supports

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const steps=[...fs.readFileSync("scripts/check.sh","utf8").matchAll(/^[ \\t]*step .*?(\.\/scripts\/[a-z-]+\.sh)/gm)].map(m=>m[1]);const gated=require("./profiles/dotagents.json").checks.filter(c=>c.gate).map(c=>c.cmd).join(" ");const missing=steps.filter(s=>!gated.includes(s));if(missing.length){console.error("not gated by profiles/dotagents.json: "+missing.join(" "));process.exit(1)}console.log("all "+steps.length+" suites check.sh runs are gated")'
checks.when: a suite added to check.sh and not to this profile is a suite the gate stops running. Counting steps would not work -- the granularities differ (shell-syntax and no-bash4 are one check.sh step; templates-valid is not a check.sh step at all), so the invariant is coverage of the scripts check.sh invokes, not equal counts. The shell-function steps (syntax, CLAUDE.md symlink, exec bits) have their own checks above; the tree-clean step is about the suites not dirtying the repo and is meaningless inside the gate.
